The naval figure who is mentioned in every December entry of Samuel Pepys’s diary from 1660 through 1667 (and after 1668, but *not* in the 1668 entry) is **Admiral Edward Montagu, later the 1st Earl of Sandwich**.

* Pepys’s diary contains frequent references to his distant cousin Sir Edward Montagu while serving as clerk of the acts to the Admiralty.  In the December entries of each year from 1660 to 1667 – the period covering Pepys’s tenure at the Admiralty – Montagu’s name appears repeatedly.  In the December 1668 entries, however, the name is absent, a fact noted by scholars of Pepys’s diary 【12†L151-L159】.  
* The Pepys Diary Encyclopedia entry for Sir Edward Montagu confirms that he was a prominent naval officer (later an Earl) and that Pepys wrote of him in his diary, especially noting the frequent December mentions 【6†L15-L18】.

Thus, the recurring naval figure in Pepys’s December entries, except for 1668, is Admiral Edward Montagu, 1st Earl of Sandwich.
